content.text: {"title":"The Moonlit Welcome","premise":"After sunset, Ada and Bo prepare a garden welcome for a shy visiting moth. Ada wants a grand shadow performance, while Bo wants the moth to feel safe. Their lamp makes beautiful shadows, but its bright circle can also frighten the guest. A tiny silver bell, a paper moon, and a patch of moonflowers give the children different ways to invite, perform, or quietly welcome their visitor.","cast_and_props":"Ada, child performer, wants a spectacular shadow show and believes the moth enjoys bright movement. Bo, child gardener, wants the moth to stay and believes it prefers stillness and moonflower scent. Pip, a shy moth, wants a gentle place to land and initially hides beneath a leaf. Props: garden gate, hand lamp, paper moon, silver bell, moonflower patch, folded welcome ribbon. State slots include pip.location, pip.content, pip.invited, ada.plan, bo.plan, lamp.brightness, lamp.owner, moon.position, bell.rung, ribbon.tied, ada.knows.pip.location, bo.knows.pip.location, ada.knows.lamp.brightness, bo.knows.lamp.brightness, and performed.mode.","kernels_and_interactions":"1. Observe/tell knowledge: a child can notice where Pip hides or how bright the lamp is; knowledge enables the correct invitation or lamp adjustment. 2. Transfer: the lamp or bell may pass between Ada and Bo, changing who can act. 3. Preparation: place the paper moon, tie the ribbon, or ring the bell, each establishing a different welcome. 4. Performance: Ada performs a moving shadow show or a still moon tableau; Pip's response depends on brightness and motion. 5. Guest response: Pip lands, hides, or follows the moonflower scent. These families interact through real ownership, knowledge, plans, and locations rather than counters.","seed_parameters":"Use seed to choose initial conditions: lamp.brightness is bright or soft; Pip begins under the moonflower leaves or behind the garden gate; Ada initially plans moving shadows or a paper-moon tableau; Bo initially plans bell invitation or scented welcome; lamp.owner is Ada or Bo. premise_keys: lamp.brightness, pip.location, ada.plan, bo.plan. Outcomes should vary physically: pip.location becomes moonflower, gate, or ribbon; pip.content becomes welcomed, startled, or curious; performed.mode becomes shadows, tableau, or none; ribbon.tied and bell.rung record concrete preparations.","candidate_scenes":"1 look_for_pip (observe Pip's location). 2 inspect_lamp (observe brightness). 3 ada_tells_pip_place (tell Ada to Bo). 4 bo_tells_lamp (tell Bo to Ada). 5 transfer_lamp_to_bo. 6 transfer_lamp_to_ada. 7 choose_moving_shadows (Ada plan). 8 choose_still_tableau (Ada plan). 9 tie_welcome_ribbon. 10 place_paper_moon. 11 ring_soft_bell. 12 scent_moonflowers. 13 soften_lamp (requires knowledge of brightness and lamp access). 14 brighten_lamp (only if Ada's plan and access justify it). 15 invite_from_gate. 16 perform_moving_shadows. 17 perform_still_tableau. 18 pip_lands_on_moonflower. 19 pip_follows_paper_moon. 20 pip_hides_after_bright_motion. Reuse look_for_pip, inspect_lamp, tie_welcome_ribbon, and final guest-response scenes across paths. The inciting action is Ada opening the garden gate and promising a welcome, which establishes Pip's possible arrival before any child responds.","constraints":"Use 2–4 characters and only the shared garden setting. Declare every slot before use; all state values are scalar and keys begin with an entity ID. Provide 12–22 candidates, with 5–10 selected events and prune=True. Use 1–2 pivotal moments: Ada changes from grand moving shadows to a gentler tableau after learning Pip's hiding place, or Bo accepts Ada's performance after seeing Pip follow the paper moon. Knowledge must be observed or told before speech or action relying on it. Pip cannot be described as understanding the plan before landing. Catalog every candidate scene, including unseen preview paths, with conditional variants. Use phrase lexicon entries for brightness, plan, location, and content. No abstract counters, project-management language, invented repairs, or explanatory moral.","different_endings":"1. Gentle tableau: Pip follows the paper moon and settles on the ribbon beside the moonflowers; the children hold their breath while its wings paint one small shadow on the gate. 2. Moonflower welcome: Pip ignores the performance but lands in the scented flowers, where Bo's bell gives one soft silver note and Ada kneels to watch. 3. Startled-but-returning: bright moving shadows send Pip behind the gate; later Pip peeks out toward the quiet ribbon, leaving the welcome unfinished but hopeful. 4. Shared spectacle: with softened light and a still tableau, Pip lands on the paper moon, making Ada's enormous shadow look like a tiny moth dancing inside it."}
